_comment: Return sentences after a foraging trip, per resource family. Placeholders: {name} character first name, {place} the mission's place (lowercase-safe), {Place} the same capitalized, {activity} the foraging name in lowercase. rich = pool still at least half full after the trip; thin = more than half depleted; depleted = this was the last trip (the site is hidden afterwards) and depletedHint is appended.
depletedHint: This location is depleted. New adventures may reveal better gathering places.

rich: {name} came back from {activity} at {place} with a satchel heavy with ore.
{name} worked {place} from dawn and hauled home good, rust-red ore.
thin: {name} searched {place}, but found little more than rust-flecked stones.
{name} spent the day {activity} at {place}, but the good ore seems to be gone.
depleted: {name} scraped the last scraps of ore from {place}. Nothing worth a pick is left there.
{Place} is picked clean; {name} gathered what little ore was left.

rich: {name} returned from {place} with an armful of sound, seasoned wood.
A good day at {place}: {name} came home dragging straight timber.
thin: {name} searched {place}, but found mostly rot and kindling.
{name} picked through {place} and found only a few usable sticks.
depleted: {name} carried home the last sound wood from {place}.
Only stumps and sawdust remain at {place}; {name} took what little wood was left.

rich: {name} came back from {place} with sacks of clean, fine sand.
{name} dug at {place} all day and filled every sack.
thin: {name} sifted {place} for hours, but most of it was mud and pebbles.
{name} searched {place}, but found almost nothing fine enough to use.
depleted: {name} sieved the last good sand from {place}.
{Place} has given up all its fine sand; {name} scraped together the last of it.

rich: {name} came back from {place} with slick lumps of good clay.
{name} dug deep at {place} and filled the baskets with clay.
thin: {name} dug at {place}, but the clay was gritty and thin.
{name} searched {place}, but found almost nothing a potter would want.
depleted: {name} pried the last workable clay from {place}.
{Place} is dug out; {name} brought back the last of its clay.

rich: {name} returned from {place} with a cart of sound stone.
{name} split good blocks at {place} all day.
thin: {name} searched {place}, but found mostly cracked and crumbling stone.
{name} spent the day at {place} and found only a few usable stones.
depleted: {name} hauled the last sound stone away from {place}.
Only rubble is left at {place}; {name} took the last good stone.

rich: {name} came back from {place} with crystals glinting in every pocket.
{name} found a rich pocket of crystal at {place}.
thin: {name} searched {place}, but found only dull chips and splinters.
{name} tapped every rock at {place}; few held any crystal.
depleted: {name} chipped the last clear crystal from {place}.
{Place} has lost its sparkle; {name} found the last of its crystal.

rich: {name} returned from {place} with a bundle of good hides.
{name} had a fine day at {place} and came home with hides to spare.
thin: {name} searched {place}, but the hides were torn and scarce.
{name} came back from {place} with only a few ragged hides.
depleted: {name} took the last decent hide from {place}.
{Place} has nothing left to skin; {name} brought home the last of it.

rich: {name} came home from {place} with a fine haul for the larder.
A good day at {place}: {name} returned with plenty of meat.
thin: {name} waited for hours at {place}, but the game had grown wary and scarce.
{name} searched {place}, but came back with barely a meal.
depleted: {name} brought back the last meat from {place}; the game has moved on.
{Place} is empty of game; {name} caught the last of it.

rich: {name} came back from {place} with baskets brimming.
{Place} was generous; {name} returned with full baskets.
thin: {name} searched {place}, but the best of it had already been picked.
{name} gleaned {place} all day and found almost nothing worth keeping.
depleted: {name} gathered the very last of the harvest from {place}.
{Place} is stripped bare; {name} found the final handful.

rich: {name} came back from {place} with a dripping, heavy catch.
The fish were biting at {place}; {name} returned with a full creel.
thin: {name} waited long at {place}, but the water gave up only small fry.
{name} fished {place} all day and caught almost nothing.
depleted: {name} pulled the last fish from {place}; the water is empty now.
{Place} is fished out; {name} landed the final catch.

rich: {name} returned from {place} with soft, fine skins.
{name} found good skins at {place} and brought plenty home.
thin: {name} searched {place}, but the skins were thin, scarred and few.
{name} came back from {place} with almost nothing fine enough to use.
depleted: {name} took the last good skin from {place}.
{Place} has no more fine skins; {name} brought back the last of them.

rich: {name} came home from {place} with bundles of good fiber.
{name} gathered strong fiber at {place} until the sacks were full.
thin: {name} searched {place}, but found only short, brittle strands.
{name} picked through {place} and found almost nothing worth spinning.
depleted: {name} pulled the last useful strands from {place}.
{Place} is picked bare; {name} found the final hank of fiber.

rich: {name} returned from {place} smelling of fresh herbs, the basket full.
{Place} was in full leaf; {name} gathered herbs aplenty.
thin: {name} searched {place}, but found only wilted and trampled leaves.
{name} combed {place} and found almost nothing worth drying.
depleted: {name} cut the last good sprigs from {place}.
{Place} is picked bare; {name} found the final sprigs.

rich: {name} came back from {place} with tall, straight bundles of reed.
{name} cut fine reed at {place} all day.
thin: {name} waded through {place}, but most of the reed was broken or rotten.
{name} searched {place} and found only a few usable stems.
depleted: {name} cut the last good stems from {place}.
{Place} is cut back to stubble; {name} took the last of the reed.

rich: {name} returned from {place} with a pouch full of fine feathers.
{name} had a lucky day at {place}: feathers everywhere.
thin: {name} searched {place}, but found only scruffy down and broken quills.
{name} came back from {place} with barely a feather worth keeping.
depleted: {name} picked up the last fine feathers at {place}.
The birds have left {place}; {name} found the last of their feathers.

rich: {name} came back from {place} with a sack of clean, sound bone.
{name} found good bone at {place} and brought plenty home.
thin: {name} searched {place}, but found mostly splinters and brittle fragments.
{name} dug around {place} and found almost nothing unbroken.
depleted: {name} took the last sound bone from {place}.
{Place} has given up its bones; {name} found the final pieces.

rich: {name} returned from {place} with a grisly, valuable haul.
{name} found strange remains aplenty at {place}.
thin: {name} searched {place}, but found only scraps of something long dead.
{name} came back from {place} with almost nothing a buyer would want.
depleted: {name} took the last strange remains from {place}.
Whatever lived around {place} is long gone; {name} found the final scraps.

both: The icy night clamped down on {name}: fingers aching, and pale ghosts walking through every dream.
A storm howled over the camp. {name} lay shivering on stony ground, haunted by restless dreams.
Frost bit through every layer, and whispers in the dark kept {name} from any real sleep.
body: {name} slept on cold, stony ground and woke stiff and aching.
The night chill crept into {name}'s bones; every joint complained at dawn.
Roots and stones dug into {name}'s back all night long.
soul: Ghostly dreams stalked {name} through the night; the morning felt hollow.
Strange whispers kept {name} half awake until first light.
{name} dreamt of pale faces at the edge of the firelight and woke uneasy.
sheltered: Wind and cold rattled the camp, but {name} slept warm and dry.
The night turned bitter, yet {name}'s camp kept the worst of it away.
calm: A mild night: {name} slept soundly under the open sky.
Warm air and a clear sky; {name} hardly missed a bed.
nights.wishNone: {name} wished for a bedroll or a tent.

sheltered: It was a cold night, but {name} kept warm in the {shelter}.
Frost settled on the grass outside; inside the {shelter}, {name} slept snug and warm.
The air bit cold after sunset, yet the {shelter} kept {name} warm till morning.
body: A damp chill crept in before dawn; {name} woke with stiff, cold fingers.
The cold ground drew the warmth from {name}'s back all night.
soul: An owl's cry and a cold mist filled {name}'s dreams with restless shapes.
{name} lay awake in the cool dark, listening to whispers that weren't the wind.

sheltered: An icy storm raged all night, but {name} stayed warm and dry in the {shelter}.
Sleet hammered the camp while {name} lay warm in the {shelter}, untouched by the cold.
The wind howled and the frost bit hard, yet {name} woke rested in the {shelter}.
body: The frost found its way to {name}'s bones; every joint ached at dawn.
Icy wind cut through the camp, and {name} woke numb and shivering.
soul: The storm screamed all night; {name} hardly slept and dreamt of drowning.
Thunder and dark visions chased each other through {name}'s restless sleep.
